brief: An appointment-based hair salon in Bristol with five stylists, cutting and colouring for regular clients who book weeks ahead.

sources.note: I want a colourist who can fix my box dye without taking too much off. I want to see their colour work before I book. I book on my phone in the evening and I need to see which Saturday slots are free. I am nervous about turning up to someone I have not met.
The shopfront has deep plum fascia with brass lettering in a high-contrast serif, and a pale blush interior visible through the window.
sources.lettering: Brass high-contrast serif lettering on a plum fascia.

sources.note: Photographs of finished colour work by each stylist, taken in the salon with the stylist's first name written in the file.

statement.object: a colourist who can correct box dye
statement.context: and book a Saturday slot without having met them

functional.value: They want a colourist who can fix their box dye without taking too much off and a free Saturday slot.

emotional.value: They are nervous about turning up to a stylist they have not met.

social.value: They want to see colour work they could show a friend before they book.

consideration.because: The visitor compares colour work and checks Saturday slots in the evening before booking weeks ahead.

objections: not seeing the colourist's work before booking
not knowing which Saturday slots are free
turning up to someone they have not met
language: I want to see their colour work before I book
I need to see which Saturday slots are free

primaryAction.because: The medium consideration job is booking a Saturday slot on a phone in the evening, so booking is offered beside each stylist's colour work as well as in the header and at the end.

order.because: A client with box dye needs to see colour work before anything else, so the first screen shows finished colour.
They want to see which colourist suits them and which Saturday slots are free, so each stylist is a card with booking beside their work.
They want to see colour work before they book, so a fuller gallery sits for those who want to look further.
A client who has seen the work and the slots can book without scrolling back to the header.

lead.because: The visitor needs a colourist who can correct box dye, so correction leads ahead of the cuts and styling the salon also does.

journey.because: A visitor with box dye first needs to see finished colour work before booking.
They compare each colourist's work and the free Saturday slots before they choose.
Once they have seen the colour work and a free slot, booking takes seconds on a phone.

proof.what: one finished box dye correction photographed in the salon
proof.because: The visitor wants to see colour work before they book, so one finished correction is the first thing met.

proof.what: each stylist's first name beside their own colour work
proof.because: A client nervous about turning up to someone they have not met can see the name and the work of the stylist they would book.

proof.what: the full gallery of colour work by every stylist
proof.because: A visitor who wants to see more colour work before they book can open the gallery, while the first screen stays short.

accent.because: The shopfront has a deep plum fascia, so the same plum colour marks the booking button.

ground.because: The shopfront shows a pale blush interior through the window, so the page ground follows that blush.

display.because: The brass high-contrast serif lettering on the shopfront gives headlines a high-contrast serif.

body.because: The brass lettering on the shopfront is paired with plain supporting text that stays easy to read.

shape.because: The fascia on the shopfront has crisp square corners, so the buttons keep them.
